subject: spanish
title: Stretch: At the Doctor's — Me Duele
welcome_lead: Stretch: visit the doctor, describe symptoms with 'doler' and body parts.
meta_desc: GCSE Spanish stretch adventure on illness, body parts and doler.
final_note: ¡Fantástico! You can now explain symptoms in Spanish.

concepts.def: It hurts me — singular thing hurts.
They hurt me — plural things hurt.

walkthroughs.body_html: Doler matches the body part, not the person. Singular: Me duele la cabeza (My head hurts). Plural: Me duelen los pies (My feet hurt). For 'his/her': Le duele el brazo. For 'we': Nos duelen los ojos.
Key body parts: la cabeza (head), la garganta (throat), el estómago, la espalda (back), el brazo, la pierna, el pie / los pies, la mano / las manos. Use definite articles (el/la), NOT possessives.

Other symptom phrases use tener: Tengo fiebre (I have a fever), Tengo tos (I have a cough), Tengo gripe (I have the flu), Estoy enfermo/a (I'm ill). At the chemist: ¿Tiene algo para la tos? (Do you have something for a cough?).

numericals.q: How many arms (brazos) does a person typically have?
